input.last_assistant_message: Cross-referencing the 4 shipped hooks against `hooks/*.sh` on disk vs the README's own claims: all 4 exist at the paths the README documents, all 4 are wired in settings.json exactly as the README's wiring table says, and diffing hooks/*.sh against `git show HEAD:hooks/*.sh` shows zero drift from the canonical repo, and all 4 pieces have genuinely fired multiple times since 2026-07-24 through today (2026-08-12) — the fixpack is live and active, not dormant. However, 3 of 4 hooks (`postfail`, `pretool`, `subagent-stop`) share the same design flaw: unanchored substring matching on tool output/messages, which produces confirmed false positives (one reproduced live in this very audit) alongside genuine detections — so raw firing counts overstate true-positive events and the counts given above (27/10/32/21) are upper bounds, not verified-true-positive counts. `rewake`'s time-parser is narrower than its README claim but fails safe (bounded fallback, never fails to eventually rewake).
